title: “I have much more to say to you, more than you can now bear.  But when he, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will guide you into all the truth. He will not speak on his own; he will speak only what he hears, and he will tell you what is yet to come. He will glorify me because it is from me that he will receive what he will make known to you. 1All that belongs to the Father is mine. That is why I said the Spirit will receive from me what he will make known to you.”
devotional:
The Spirit of truth encourages intimacy.

Look at what Jesus said, ‘He will glorify me because it is from me that he will receive what he will make known to you.’ In other words the Holy Spirit makes the truth about Jesus a reality. As the Holy Spirit works in our lives Jesus will become more real to us, and the things that are important to Jesus will become important to us.

The truth is, Jesus is the ultimate ‘truth experience’ every man, woman and child needs to know, and this ‘truth experience’ is only realized when the Spirit guides us into all truth. So the Holy Spirit wants to make Jesus a permanent reality to us. I cannot think of anything more wonderful than knowledge of the reality of Jesus.

Integrity and intimacy are linked. Have you ever gone up to someone you wanted a better friendship/relationship with and say something like. ‘I would really love to get to know you better, so in order for that to happen why don’t we become more superficial, let’s pretend, and not be real and ensure that we keep our masks on;, avoid the truth and that will help us to know each other better.’

We would never say that, but that is often how we treat each other. But even more serious is this, our lack of integrity with others affects our intimacy with Jesus.

Would you befriend someone who was unreal? Someone who was always putting on a performance? Would you share your heart and life with someone who you knew was always wearing a persona to hide his or her true thoughts and feelings from others, someone who has no interest in genuine relationships? Of course not. Do you think Jesus would like a relationship with that kind of person? Someone who is not real, someone who is always pretending?

Jesus loves broken sinful people, but he has very little time for people who are fake who will not be honest about themselves. Jesus loves reality. The Spirit of truth comes to expose the hidden, and in doing so makes us more open to receive a true experience of Jesus. It is sad to think that the masks many Christians wear are the masks that blind them from really seeing Jesus.

The Holy Spirit will guide us into all truth. It would be very easy for us to miss the impact of this statement. The word guide is used only five times in the New Testament, twice in the writings of John, and only here in his gospel. I don’t think we really consider guidance into truth as being a priority. I think we would rather be guided into some kind of plan or purpose than be guided into truth; truth about ourselves and truth about God. Let me try and make this more practical. Can you think of a truth that God has helped you to understand? One that has led you to make changes in how you live and what you live for? The path God guides us on will include God’s plans and purposes, but his plans and purposes are not his priority. His priority is to lead us into truth so we can be transformed for intimacy with him.
prayer: Father thank you that to be guided into truth is more important than to be guided into your plans.
